description:
Programme or Project Overview

The Department of Mathematics at Aarhus University invites applications for PhD positions in mathematics, statistics and stochastics within its graduate programme. The call covers projects across the department's research groups, including analysis, geometry, probability, statistics and applied mathematics, with successful candidates joining active research environments at the Aarhus campus. Positions are salaried under the Danish collective agreement, so no external funding is required.

Doctoral students work on an individual research plan agreed with their supervisor, complete coursework within the Graduate School framework, and contribute to teaching in later years of the programme. The standard PhD track runs for three years, with an option for five-year tracks that include integrated master's study where offered. The department's PhD school provides office space, computing resources, travel support for conferences and research visits, and an international seminar culture.

Research environment

Aarhus mathematics has a strong international profile, with groups working across pure and applied topics and close cooperation with the department's statistics and data science activities. PhD students participate in the department's seminar and workshop programme, collaborate across groups and often spend research stays with partners abroad. Applicants normally hold a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS) in mathematics or a closely related field with a substantial thesis component, and admission is assessed on academic qualifications, research experience and the match with available supervision capacity.

Highlights

  • Pure mathematics: analysis, geometry and topology
  • Probability theory and stochastic processes
  • Mathematical statistics and data science
  • Applied and computational mathematics
  • Salaried three-year PhD track under Danish collective agreement
  • International seminar programme and travel support
